document_title: The Every-day Life of Abraham Lincoln: A Narrative And Descriptive Biography With Pen-Pictures And Personal; Recollections By Those Who Knew Him
author: Francis F. Browne
claims: Lincoln entered the chamber shortly after twelve o'clock and joined the procession to the eastern portico.
As Lincoln took the oath of office, sunlight burst from the clouds, illuminating him.
Lincoln stated that the sunburst made his heart jump.
The address was described as eloquent and imperishable.
Lincoln noted that at his second appearance for the oath, there was less occasion for an extended address than at the first.
He stated that much new information could not be presented due to public declarations on the contest over the past four years.
The progress of arms was known to the public and reasonably satisfactory and encouraging.
No predictions for the future were ventured.
Four years prior, all thoughts were directed to an impending civil war, which all sought to avoid.
While the inaugural address was being delivered, insurgent agents were in the city seeking to destroy the Union with war.
The address was devoted almost exclusively to the attempt of the Southern States to withdraw from the Union.
The address contained a calm, firm, moderate, and judicious spirit.
Lincoln quoted himself, stating he had no purpose to interfere with slavery in the states where it existed and believed he had no lawful right to do so.
The address included the famous phrase, 'With malice toward none, with charity for all'.
The address was delivered from the eastern portico.
Lincoln's address did not disarm personal resentment from the South or sufficiently strengthen Union-loving people there against secessionists.
